title: Pool depletion failures: root cause analysis and hotfix for burst allocation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported sudden failures to obtain burst capacity from reserved pools during high-throughput windows. Requests were rejected with 429/503 when the control plane reported available headroom. This ticket drives root cause analysis, a staging hotfix rollout, and follow-up reliability improvements.
symptoms: Observed rejected allocation traces from dedicated control plane with 'insufficient_headroom' while dashboard showed available pool capacity
Customers saw increased tail latency and 429 throttles for short bursts (1-3 minutes) across two regions
Autoscaler attempted scale-up but new nodes did not receive allocations due to a race in allocation bookkeeping
root_cause_summary: Race between burst allocation path and node deallocation: in-flight allocations were not reflected atomically in pool.available units
Control plane cached 'available' values with eventual consistency; scaling(decision)->provision path assumed immediate consistency and double-counted capacity
A rounding/truncation bug in the burst headroom math caused underestimation of required extra instances for certain VM sizes under mixed-tenant workloads
Telemetry showed a sharp spike in concurrent allocation attempts during customer traffic surge exposing the race
steps_taken: Mounted urgent on-call triage 2026-03-12 08:12 UTC; collected allocation traces and request IDs from affected customers
Reproduced allocation race locally with a synthetic load generator that submitted concurrent burst requests to reserved pools
Applied emergency staging hotfix: switched pool.available updates to use a compare-and-swap (CAS) / optimistic locking approach, preventing double allocation in the window
Rolled hotfix to two canary dedicated clusters in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 and monitored error rate/latency for 45m
Validated with customers (acct-7632 and acct-9145) who confirmed absence of 429s during repeated burst tests
resolution: Hotfix deployed to control plane: allocation bookkeeping moved to atomic update path; headroom math fixed to use ceil() for instance-based capacity and test coverage added. Canary metrics indicate errors dropped to baseline. Full rollout scheduled after postmortem reviews.
